Posted By: Blair McBride November 6, 2026
Rare earth developers are turning to the U.S. South’s chemical plants, ports and mineral deposits to build a supply chain that can compete with China. Louisiana is drawing three processing ventures, while explorers in Georgia and elsewhere in the region look for deposits that could eventually supply them.
Aclara Resources (TSX: ARA) received a non-binding letter of interest in September for up to $750 million (C$1 billion) from the U.S. Export-Import Bank to finance its proposed Dynamo separation plant in Louisiana. The company plans to feed it with material from projects in Chile and Brazil.
“The market is being pushed by two sides,” Aclara CEO Ramón Barúa told The Northern Miner . “The Chinese continue to restrict the rare earths, and on the other side, the Western world continues to also try to limit their use of Chinese [rare earth] product. We are the centre of those two converging forces.”
The Gulf Coast offers ports to bring in feedstock and a chemical industry with the workers and suppliers to process it. The test is whether developers can secure financing and enough material to keep separation plants running reliably at commercial scale.
Louisiana cluster
Aclara aims to start site preparation for its $494-million Dynamo plant in the first quarter of 2027, subject to financing. It targets construction completion in the second half of 2028. The site is at the Port of Vinton, about 340 km west of New Orleans.
Dynamo would process material from Aclara’s Penco project in Chile, whose first stage has environmental approval, and Carina in Brazil, which is awaiting environmental licences. Both host rare earths in shallow ionic clays that require no blasting, crushing or grinding, the company says.
Aclara is testing its separation technology at a demonstration plant in Blacksburg, Va. A second demonstration plant, which opened in Chile in October, is testing technology to make metals and alloys.
At full capacity, Dynamo could produce annual averages of about 1,300 tonnes of neodymium-praseodymium oxide, 200 tonnes of dysprosium oxide and 35 tonnes of terbium oxide, according to Aclara’s October engineering update. The company has added yttrium, gadolinium and samarium to its planned product range.
Canada’s Ucore Rare Metals (TSXV: UCU; US-OTC: UURAF) is installing equipment at its separation plant in Alexandria, La., and has secured $27 million in federal defence funding. ElementUSA plans to recover rare earths from bauxite residue at the Atlantic Alumina refinery in Gramercy, La. It received a $29.9-million defence award for gallium and scandium recovery and is part of a Colorado School of Mines-led project selected for negotiations over $67 million in Department of Energy funding.
Ucore and ElementUSA did not respond to requests for comment before this article was published in the November print issue of The Northern Miner .
Operating at scale
Aclara chose Louisiana for access to chemical suppliers and to operators and contractors with petrochemical experience around Lake Charles, Barúa said.
Dynamo would use about 500 mixer-settlers, which separate metals using solvents. Material can take months to move through the system, so operators may wait a long time to see the effect of adjustments, Barúa said.
“The hardest part, by far, is operating these facilities,” he said. “Ramping up and then having stable production is going to be very, very difficult to attain.”
Processing the feedstock in Brazil and Chile before it reaches Louisiana should help stabilize separation at Dynamo, Barúa said. Aclara is using its pilot plant to gain operating experience before scaling up.
Aclara shares were 15% weaker at C$2.05 at Thursday’s close in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$601 million.
Georgia feedstock
Rare Earths Americas (NYSE-A: REA) is drilling its Foothills project about 110 km southwest of Atlanta. The company also holds three projects in Brazil, including Alpha and Constellation, which have initial resources. Gina Rinehart’s Hancock Prospecting held about 6% of the explorer through subsidiary Hanrine Investments, according to a September filing.
The company is conducting a 25,000- to 30,000-metre drill program at Foothills and plans to release an initial resource in the first quarter of 2027, CEO Don Swartz told The Northern Miner .
The Gulf Coast’s ports and transport links allow processors to bring in concentrates while domestic mining projects advance, Swartz said.
“You’re seeing a cluster along the coast where you’re able to import concentrates and… process them,” he said. “The Gulf Coast, for instance, in the Texas area [has] good transportation and government support.”
Rare Earths Americas acquired Shiloh in July 2025 when it bought Australia’s Foothills Rare Earths. It outlined the 1,650-sq.-km Foothills district a year later, comprising Shiloh, Liberty Peak and three other targets. Land and access agreements remain to be finalized on some prospective ground.
Drill hole 25-DPLC-022 cut 10.2 metres grading 2.02% total rare earth oxides from surface, the company reported June 15. Mineralization occurs in saprolite clays and monazite-bearing sands. The project sits on private land and would require state approvals and potentially federal permits to develop.
Processing options
Monazite from Foothills could potentially be processed at Energy Fuels’ (TSX: EFR; NYSE-A: UUUU) White Mesa mill in Utah or at the Saskatchewan Research Council’s plant in Saskatoon, Swartz said. White Mesa already uses monazite feed, including material from Chemours’ (NYSE: CC) operations in the South. It has produced neodymium-praseodymium oxide commercially and dysprosium and terbium oxides at pilot scale.
Elsewhere in the region, USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) has a feasibility study under way at Round Top in Texas. IperionX (ASX: IPX) completed a feasibility study in June for its Titan project in Tennessee. Chemours extracts mineral sands containing rare earths in Florida and Georgia.
Rare Earths Americas shares were 12% weaker at $7.25 at Thursday’s close in New York, valuing the company at about $149 million based on the share count at print time.
“We’ve got a very large pack­age that we’re drilling out, and we see widespread mineralization,” Swartz said. “You start with the proof of concept and then you grow the resource every time.”

While Moderna preps an entry to the oncology market next year with a personalized cancer vaccine, COVID sales are holding steady with several other vaccine launches underway around the world.
While several Big Pharmas have reported declining vaccine rates that have eaten into sales, mRNA bigwig Moderna is seeing steady revenue from its COVID-19 shots thanks to global adoption.
Moderna’s revenue grew 29% to $1.3 billion for the quarter, compared to $1 billion for the same period a year earlier. The company has so far totaled $1.8 billion in revenue this year, CFO Jamey Mock said on a Friday morning earnings call . He attributed this jump to higher COVID vaccine sales, with mNEXSPIKE and Spikevax available globally for the coming season.
“In the U.S., while the vaccination season is still ongoing, we have seen increased uptake of mNEXSPIKE, and vaccination rates have been relatively stable versus the prior year,” Mock said.
The U.S. has been a tough market for vaccines over the past two seasons amid political hampering that have spurred declining rates, as reported by major drugmakers like GSK and Pfizer .
Pfizer, which marketed Comirnaty with partner BioNTech, reported declining sales across its COVID franchise, which also includes the treatment Paxlovid.
Despite Mock’s reported increase in uptake for mNEXSPIKE, U.S. revenue for the product is overall declining, with the global expansion leading Moderna’s sales there, Jefferies noted. Moderna could gain more market share once Pfizer’s contract in the EU expires at the end of this year, the firm said.
Moderna did not return a request for clarification on the COVID product sales as of publication.
Jefferies attributed the COVID vaccine strength in the quarter to “favorable COVID seasonality.” Vaccinations typically pick up in the third quarter, when Moderna generally records the bulk of its vaccine revenue for the year.
Moderna did not provide specific sales numbers for the COVID shots but vaccine sales overall totaled $1.27 billion, higher than consensus of $891 million, William Blair said in a Friday morning note. That number would also include mRESVIA for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), mFLUSIVA and mCOFLU, which became available in some global markets this year.
“Both the U.S. and international markets delivered stronger than expected revenue in 3Q, driven by a mix of increased demand, operational execution and timing of shipments between the third and fourth quarters,” Mock said.

Tesla has raised Cybertruck prices in the US by up to 10% and stopped taking orders for the base Dual Motor AWD trim. The cheapest Cybertruck you can actually order now costs $92,490.
The move comes right after Tesla confirmed it will end Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027.
The new Cybertruck prices
Here’s what Tesla’s online configurator shows today, compared to the prices set in August:
Dual Motor AWD: $82,490, up from $74,990 (+$7,500, 10%), but no longer orderable
Premium AWD: $92,490, up from $84,990 (+$7,500, 8.8%)
Cyberbeast: $102,490, up from $99,990 (+$2,500, 2.5%)
The Dual Motor trim still shows a new, higher price on Tesla’s website, but the option is greyed out. So Tesla raised the price of a version it isn’t selling anymore.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
This is the second price hike in less than three months. Tesla raised prices by $5,000 on two trims in August , when the Dual Motor went from $69,990 to $74,990 and the Premium AWD from $79,990 to $84,990.
Add it up and the Premium AWD is now $12,500 (15.6%) more expensive than it was in early August. And the entry price for any Cybertruck you can order went from $69,990 to $92,490. That’s a 32% jump in about 10 weeks.
For reference, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in 2019 with a promised starting price of $39,900.
Higher prices on a truck nobody’s buying
The price hikes make little sense from a demand standpoint. Tesla doesn’t break out Cybertruck deliveries, but its “Other Models” category, which also includes the Model S, Model X, and Semi, fell 48% year-over-year to 8,295 units in Q3. We estimate Cybertrucks made up 7,000 to 8,000 of those, about 12% of the line’s 250,000-unit annual capacity.
Tesla also tried the opposite approach earlier this year. It offered a dual-motor Cybertruck at $59,990 in February for “only the next 10 days,” then pulled it. A single-motor RWD version was discontinued after just 173 sales. None of it moved the needle.
The Cybertruck isn’t sold in Europe or most right-hand-drive markets, and Tesla canceled it for Australia and New Zealand last month.

Once you’ve decided to end a program, volume stops mattering. You have a set number of build slots left, a parts supply you want to burn down, and probably a small group of fans who’ll want one before it’s gone. Pausing the cheapest trim and charging $7,500 more for the rest is the obvious play. You push everyone into higher-margin configurations and stop pretending the base truck is a real product.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne show off the 2026 federal budget Nov. 5 in Ottawa. Credit: François-Philippe Champagne via X.
By: Colin McClelland and Frederic Tomesco November 6, 2026
Ottawa’s five-year extension of mineral exploration tax credits has won praise from Canada’s prospectors association, but British Columbia’s exploration group says the budget misses a key change needed to help discoveries become mines.
Thursday’s federal budget proposes keeping the 15% Mineral Exploration Tax Credit and 30% Critical Mineral Exploration Tax Credit available through March 31, 2032, providing an estimated $956 million (US$684 million) in support over five years. Ottawa also proposes $424.4 million over four years, starting in 2027-28, to renew the Canadian Critical Minerals Strategy.
“Extending both credits for five years responds directly to PDAC’s call for greater long-term certainty and gives explorers more confidence to plan and finance work across multiple field seasons,” Jeff Killeen, senior director of policy and programs at the Prospectors & Developers Association of Canada, told The Northern Miner in e-mailed comments.
Both PDAC and the Association for Mineral Exploration have sought expanded Canadian Exploration Expense eligibility to cover engineering, economic and feasibility studies needed to establish reserves and make mine-development decisions. That remains an unmet industry request , leaving a financing gap between discovery and development, according to AME.
‘Disappointed’
“We are disappointed that Budget 2026 missed an opportunity to take the steps needed to unlock Canada’s critical minerals,” AME president and CEO Todd Stone said in an e-mailed statement. “This budget does not address that gap.”
“This budget includes measures to help early-stage technology companies access capital,” he said. “We need the same level of support for mineral exploration companies.”
The flow-through share system has generated more than two-thirds of early-stage domestic exploration activity over the past decade, according to PDAC’s analysis, Killeen said. The association had sought permanent credits or extensions of at least 10 years.
“But for too long, Canada has fallen behind in bringing those minerals from mine to market,” Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said in Parliament. “That is why we are focused on increasing Canadian production and processing of our minerals.”
Beyond exploration, the package offers power, infrastructure and financing measures that could help projects move towards construction. Much of the larger funding architecture, however, was announced before budget day.
Windfall funds spending
Ottawa projects a $62.3-billion deficit in 2026-27, up from $39.3 billion last year but about $3 billion below April’s forecast, with annual shortfalls continuing through 2030-31. Federal debt is forecast to reach $1.37 trillion this fiscal year and $1.59 trillion by the end of that period, remaining around 40% of gross domestic product. Annual debt-servicing costs would rise to $85.5 billion from $60.2 billion over the same period, according to the Department of Finance.
Improved economic and fiscal conditions provide $158 billion over five years, almost all absorbed by $152 billion in new spending, RBC economists Cynthia Leach and Salim Zanzana said in a budget analysis . Higher revenues, supported by oil prices and a stronger starting position, account for about 70% of the improvement; lower projected program expenses provide the rest, they said.
The gains from Ottawa’s investment agenda remain uncertain and will take time, while higher day-to-day spending could reduce room for future investments, Leach and Zanzana warned.
Exploration runway
Both credits expire next March 31. The budget would extend them to eligible flow-through share agreements signed by March 31, 2032, and add antimony to the 30% credit for agreements signed after budget day.
Flow-through shares allow companies to pass eligible expenses to investors as tax deductions. The credits offer an additional incentive for individuals financing grassroots exploration in Canada.
The renewed critical minerals strategy would support mining and processing technology, geoscience and research, and targeted funding for priority projects. Ottawa also proposes $34 million over four years, starting in 2027-28, to renew GeoNorth, which provides public geoscience information for northern exploration, infrastructure planning and environmental assessments.
“Public geoscience is fundamental to mineral exploration in Canada,” Killeen said. “PDAC welcomes Budget 2026’s investment in geoscience capacity because it will help attract exploration investment and support the next generation of mineral discoveries.”
Helium producers would receive separate relief. Ottawa proposes treating eligible helium exploration, development and resource-property acquisition expenses like those in conventional oil and gas, effective for spending incurred on or after budget day. The government estimates the change would provide $54 million in tax relief over four years from 2027-28.
Power and processing
For miners and processors seeking reliable electricity, the budget proposes extending the Clean Technology and Clean Electricity investment tax credits to the end of 2040. The clean technology credit’s reduction to 15% would occur in 2040 instead of 2034.
Eligibility for the clean electricity credit would also expand to the highest-voltage transmission lines within each province, for property acquired and available for use on or after budget day. That could help finance infrastructure serving new mines and industrial developments.
Further eligibility details are still pending, and draft legislation to implement the changes wasn’t released with the budget, lawyers at Osler, Hoskin & Harcourt noted.
Ottawa proposes nearly $4 billion over 10 years, starting in 2027-28, for electricity infrastructure, renewable energy and priority power projects. A further $37 million in 2027-28 would support analysis of interprovincial connections and discussions about sharing their costs.
“We’re working with provinces, territories, and Indigenous partners to double Canada’s grid capacity by 2050,” Champagne said. “We will connect provincial grids. We will build thousands of kilometres of transmission lines. We will develop the nuclear energy sector.”
Canadian industrial suppliers could benefit from proposed domestic-content bonuses. The government plans 60 days of consultations on additions of up to 10 percentage points to the clean technology credit and five percentage points to the clean electricity credit. Their scope and conditions remain to be determined.
The budget also reaffirms the Productivity Mega Deduction announced in September. It would permanently allow immediate writeoffs for a broader range of capital assets and increase the deduction rate for Canadian development expenses to 100% from 30% on a declining-balance basis. The government puts the economy-wide fiscal cost at $36 billion over five years.
Mining investors wouldn’t qualify for every new incentive. The proposed Canada Growth Incentive would exempt up to $15 million in capital gains per qualifying individual per business, subject to eligibility conditions, but the tax annex explicitly excludes mining businesses. Utilities, financial services and several other sectors are also excluded.
Approval to construction
Ottawa is proposing $187.4 million over five years from 2026-27, plus $24.2 million in future years, to launch and operate a major projects management entity and begin supporting the Mackenzie Valley Highway and Taltson Hydro Expansion in the Northwest Territories.
The entity would provide technical and project-development expertise to help approved projects advance.
The proposed one-year federal approval deadline would start once proponents submit all required studies and information. Indigenous rights, consultation duties and treaty obligations would remain intact, Ottawa says.
For project financing, the budget sets out the structure of the Canada Strong Fund, announced in the spring economic update. Ottawa plans to seed it with $25 billion over three years and introduce legislation establishing an arm’s-length Crown corporation.
The fund would invest alongside private capital on commercial terms. An illustrative model pairs a Canada Infrastructure Bank infrastructure loan with a fund investment in a critical minerals developer; no specific project investment was announced.
Bank merger
Ottawa also proposes merging Export Development Canada and the Business Development Bank of Canada into a single federal development bank, combining support for domestic growth and international expansion. A specially constituted board would oversee the transition, with existing products and services maintained.
The government expects its financing Crown corporations to take greater risks than private lenders, potentially widening financing options for mining, processing and infrastructure projects.
Such financing also makes the headline deficit an incomplete measure of Ottawa’s borrowing needs. Loans, equity investments and large capital purchases require cash upfront without all being recorded immediately as budget expenses, TD economists Beata Caranci, Francis Fong and Andrew Hencic said. Debt-servicing costs would consume about 14% of federal revenues by 2030-31, up from 11% this fiscal year, they noted.
For tariff-hit processors and manufacturers, Ottawa says support under the Regional Tariff Response Initiative has reached nearly $3.5 billion, including additional assistance for steel, copper and aluminum. The program offers support for productivity improvements, market diversification and liquidity.
Ottawa identifies more than $44.6 billion in critical minerals projects under construction or with completed impact or environmental assessments, using 2025 data and selected 2026 projects. The exploration and power measures aim to expand that pipeline and move more projects into production. Print

Mattel Launches Hot Wheels Racer Series Cars So Small and Cheap They'll Be Impossible to Ignore
8 photos
Photo: Mattel
Last year, toy maker Mattel decided to take the fight into LEGO's backyard by launching a new line of products called Brick Shop. The range of available products has constantly been growing ever since, and it presently counts tens of products. Until this week, though, there was no real entry-level line of toys available.
That changed after the company announced the release of the Hot Wheels Racer Series, a collection that blends together the Mattel way of doing things in plastic brick form with the glamour of Hot Wheels die-cast cars.
The collection that was launched this week counts no less than six vehicles, but the range is expected to grow to count as many as 20 models by the end of next year. They are all 1:64-scale, some of the smallest Brick Shop sets around, and so diverse they might very well make your head spin.
The collection includes, for instance, one of the most iconic models in Hot Wheels' history, the mighty Bone Shaker, which needs the correct assembly of 28 pieces of plastic to come together.
Then, from the 1990s, Mattel brings to life the 1991 Acura NSX (29 pieces) and the 1999 Honda S2000 (29 pieces). From closer to our time, the 2018 Audi TT RS enters the collection with 29 pieces, and so does the 29-piece 2024 Chevrolet Camaro ZL1. Finally, the Maserati MCPura wraps up the collection with 27 plastic pieces.
The above sets are entry-level not only on account of the number of pieces they require to come together, but also on account of their price. Every single one of them costs just $4.99, dirt cheap in the world of plastic brick toys.
Each of the six models will be offered complete with a metal base plate. Their wheels, fitted on metal axles, spin, and they are shod in rubber tires meant to bring them closer to their real-life siblings. Finally, each of the cars in this collection comes with its own distinct, custom pieces, that come together.
Mattel says the first examples in the Hot Wheels Racer Series will become available in January 2027, so a bit too late for parents and kids to enjoy them this Christmas. The launch dates for the remaining 14 models have not been announced yet, but we'll keep an eye on things and report back once we know more.
Those who wish to gift something from Mattel Brick Shop to their loved ones still have plenty of options available, including the recently introduced Mattel Brick Shop Original XBOX Console. The 1:1 replica of the original Microsoft XBOX from a quarter of a century ago is, obviously, a lot more expensive, selling for $329.99, and throws 3,509 plastic bricks onto the table to be properly assembled.

Kia is expanding its electric van lineup with the PV7, a larger PV5 sibling that can carry nine people or a whole lot of cargo.
The Kia PV7 van is launching in 2027
The PV5, Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business, is proving to be a bigger hit than expected.
A year after it went on sale, the PV5 quickly became Europe’s most popular small electric van. In the first half of 2026, it was the top seller in its segment, accounting for 37% of electric C-segment van sales across Europe.
Next year, Kia will launch the PV7, the second electric van from its PBV business. Kia revealed the PV7 at IAA Transportation in Hanover, Germany, in September.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
It’s based on the same E-GMP.S platform as the PV5, but the PV7 features a considerably longer wheelbase and stretched body, opening up more space inside.
The PV7 is over 17.5 ft long, measuring 5,350 mm long, 1,995 mm wide, and 1,990 mm high, with a 3,500 mm wheelbase. In comparison, the PV5 is just 4,695 mm long, 1,895 mm wide, and 1,915 mm tall, with a 2,995 mm wheelbase.
That’s even bigger than the Volkswagen ID. Buzz Long-Wheelbase (LWB), which measures 4,962 mm in length with a 3,239 mm wheelbase.
Kia PV7 Passenger (Source: Kia)
23 different top hats coming
Like the PV5, the PV7 will initially be available in Passenger and Cargo body styles, but Kia plans to launch 23 different variants, or “top hats,” over the next few years.
It will be offered with two nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) battery packs: 71.5 kWh and 96.2 kWh. The Long Range Cargo model offers an all-electric WLTP range of over 460 km (285 miles). Even at full capacity, Kia said the new PV7 achieves nearly 400 km (248 miles) of range and still has 350 liters of trunk space.
A plena capacidad la nueva #PV7 consigue casi 400 km de autonomía y aún reserva 350 litros de maletero #Kia #KiaPV7 #MovementThatInspires pic.twitter.com/fzIvviYZuE — @KiaPrensa_ES (@KiaPrensa_ES) November 4, 2026
Front-wheel drive (FWD) will be standard at launch, but Kia plans to add an all-wheel drive (AWD) option later.
Depending on the configuration, the FWD electric powertrain delivers up to 268 horsepower (200 kW) and 309 lb-ft (420 Nm) of torque.
Thanks to its 800V architecture, the Kia PV7’s battery can charge from 10% to 80% in about 25 minutes with a 350 kW DC fast charger. It will be Kia’s first vehicle with two charging ports, including a front AC/DC port and an optional rear side AC port.
Kia PV7 Cargo (left) and Passenger (right) Source: Kia)
With vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, it can serve as a mobile power source for tools, equipment, a campsite, or other external electronic devices.
Personal and business use
The PV7 Cargo, designed for businesses, fleets, and logistics, is available in 2- and 3-seat configurations and offers up to 6.1 cubic meters of cargo space. The High Roof variant offers even more, with up to 8 cubic meters.
Maximum payload is up to 1,165 kg (2,568 lbs) for the Cargo Long and up to 1,200 kg (2,645 lbs) for the compact model.
The PV7 Cargo Long features a 550 mm loading height and, according to Kia, enough capacity for up to three Euro pallets (800 x 1,200 mm). An added heavy-duty mode adjusts the vehicle’s response to varying payloads to help maintain stability and control while driving.
Depending on the use, buyers can choose between full-open twin-swing tailgate doors or a lift-up tailgate.
The PV7 Passenger, on the other hand, is designed for personal use and families, or can also be used as a shuttle with room for up to nine passengers in the global version. In Korea, it will seat up to 11 passengers.
The 7-seater features Long-Rail Easy Remove Seats, enabling various interior seating configurations. The 9-seater variant, on the other hand, is available with or without a fourth row.
High-tech and spacious interior
Inside, both versions feature Hyundai’s new Pleos Connect infotainment system, with 12.9″ and 14.6″ display screens and physical controls for commonly used functions.
The system runs Android Automotive OS, making it more like a smartphone with apps and customizable screens. It also includes Hyundai’s Gleo AI, an AI-powered in-car companion that can answer questions, control navigation or vehicle functions, and more.
Kia said the PV7 is based on a “Mobile Workspace” concept, with a layered dashboard and center console to optimize space.
The Kia PV7 Passenger and Cargo will go on sale in Korea and Europe in the second half of 2027. It will then roll out to new markets with new derivatives and conversions.
Kia will announce PV7 prices closer to its launch. In Korea, the PV5 Passenger and Cargo Compact starts at 45.9 million won ($34,000) and 41 million won ($30,000), respectively. In Germany, the PV5 Passenger 5-seater starts at €38,690 ($43,000).

X-70 Fractal Is the Next NASA Experimental Aircraft, Teaser Makes It Look Like a Stealth Fighter
64 photos
Photo: NASA
American space agency NASA has a very long tradition with experimental aircraft, as over the years it has used a whole bunch of them to advance both its expansion into space and the evolution of the aviation industry here on Earth. And the tradition is likely to continue, not only with its most recent X-plane, the X-59, but also with the upcoming X-70 Fractal.
The name was dropped for the first time earlier this week, during the UP.Summit at the NASA Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Wednesday. Accompanying it was a single image, a generated teaser showing the silhouette of an aircraft lost in smoke or fog, looking more like a stealth fighter jet than a benign, experimental aircraft.
The name of the plane follows NASA's established naming strategy, with X standing for experimental, 70 the number of the plane in the series, and Fractal - well, it's a mystery why this word, which usually stands for a geometric shape with a detailed structure at arbitrarily small scales, was chosen.
Described as a high-performance, highly adaptable research platform, the plane will be a piloted one, and it will be built in such a way as to have rapidly reconfigurable flight controls. This will allow the people behind the project to test things like aircraft maneuverability in ways that have never been possible before with humans inside an aircraft.
Naturally, NASA gave no further details on what that is supposed to mean, but it was mildly generous when it comes to the other capabilities of the aircraft. It shared, for instance, that it will be capable of carrying up to 2,000 pounds (907 kg) of payloads, held in a swappable fashion both inside and outside its body.
The plane's takeoff weight stands at 10,000 pounds (4,536 kg), and in flight it should be capable of reaching subsonic speeds of Mach .75 (575 mph/926 mph) and altitudes of up to 45,000 feet (13,700 meters).
NASA did not say what kind of engines will power the plane , or how many of them will be on board, but it did reveal they should be capable of taking the plane to distances of up to 1,726 miles (2.777 km) from its departure point.
The numbers above are exactly what NASA needs to accelerate the development and testing of new and innovative aviation technologies across a broad range of operating conditions. It'll be a long time, though, until it gets to do that, as the aircraft isn’t scheduled to fly for the first time until sometime in 2030.
We will keep an eye on things over the next months in the hope that NASA will reveal more about the X-70 Fractal project, including who has been tasked with making it and what will power it.

The BioSpace 40 Under 40 honoree helped steer Forge’s sale to Ajinomoto. Now, Samantha Piteri-Molina sees opportunities in AI-driven analytics and Ohio’s gene therapy ecosystem—with a responsibility to patients worldwide.
As vice president of business and strategy at Forge Biologics, Samantha Piteri-Molina is focused on more than just growing the manufacturing business—it’s about getting gene therapies into the hands of waiting patients, she told BioSpace .
Piteri-Molina, a BioSpace 40 Under 40 honoree, helped guide the contract development and manufacturing organization through its $620 million acquisition by Ajinomoto in late 2023. Now operating as a subsidiary of the Japanese multinational food and biotechnology corporation, Forge has been able to accelerate its commercial manufacturing ambitions, expanding to more than 425 employees while maintaining a retention rate above 92%, she said. That’s up from the 327 Forge employees as of July 2023, according to an Ajinomoto presentation .
As the CDMO grows, Piteri-Molina sees opportunities to improve how the sector works—from analyzing complex manufacturing data to drawing on the specialized talent surrounding Forge’s Ohio home.
The CDMO supports adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapy development and commercial manufacturing. Just last year, the cell and gene therapy arena achieved three new blockbuster products —Bristol Myers Squibb’s Breyanzi, Johnson & Johnson and Legend Biotech’s Carvykti and Sarepta Therapeutics’ Elevidys—bringing the total number of drugs with blockbuster status in the space to five, according to the Alliance of Regenerative Medicine (ARM).
Samantha Piteri-Molina
Piteri-Molina said she is seeing more programs advance through the clinical pathway than ever before. And “we’re seeing more drug approvals, she continued,” adding that more can still be done to improve manufacturing efficiency in the sector.
Finding AI’s value beyond ChatGPT
For Piteri-Molina, one near-term opportunity is using artificial intelligence to improve the data that gene therapy manufacturers already produce.
“There’s so much data in gene therapy manufacturing, and so I think there’s a real opportunity in how we collect it, how we analyze it, how we interpret it, that can create a lot of efficiencies,” she explained.
As manufacturers get better at making more of the vectors used to deliver gene therapies, they also need faster, more sophisticated ways to understand the product and perform quality checks. With AI, “I think that that is very achievable near-term and very valuable,” Piteri-Molina said.
Drawing on her past experiences working at PTC Therapeutics and Agios Pharmaceuticals, Piteri-Molina also sees a lot of potential for AI on the drug development side. Whether that be construct optimization or developing unique assays to pair with programs, she’s keeping her eye on how AI improves that side of biopharma.
Meanwhile, she thinks the myriad variations of Claude or ChatGPT are overhyped, drawing a distinction between tools that tackle technical challenges and the proliferation of general bots.
“There’s more diversification in those platforms that can add value, but that’s where I think: Is that the most bang for our buck in this space right now?”

Forge’s Ohio advantage
Technology is only one part of the equation. Location is another.
Forge is based in Columbus, Ohio—a hotspot for cell and gene therapy. A 2023 ARM report featured Columbus as one of 10 U.S. hubs for the sector, highlighting the city’s strong education system, low cost of living and cheap land.
“We’re really fortunate to be part of an ecosystem that grew out of the research at Nationwide Children’s Hospital, which is here in Columbus, and that a lot of that research in spun-out companies directly contributed to four FDA-approved gene therapies,” Piteri-Molina said. Those therapies are Sarepta’s Duchenne muscular dystrophy treatment Elevidys; Novartis’ spinal muscular atrophy treatments Zolgensma and Itvisma; and, most recently, Ultragenyx’s Fayuvi for Sanfilippo syndrome type A.
“That research has helped attract a lot of really specialized talent in the area that really understand the complexities of gene therapy development and manufacturing, and Forge has been able to capitalize on that talent and that ecosystem,” Piteri-Molina said.
Being located in the Midwest also gives Forge a supply chain advantage, she added.
“We’re a one-day drive for most of the U.S. population major cities along major transportation distribution networks,” Piteri-Molina explained. Those factors play a significant role in gene therapy manufacturing, which uses specialized raw materials that require temperature-controlled shipments and tight timelines.

Plug-and-play gene therapy: FDA executes on vision that’s been in the works for years
Former biologics boss Peter Marks had a vision. With the FDA’s latest draft guidance, it’s coming to fruition. Speaking with BioSpace, current CBER leader Karim Mikhail said the “adapted pathway” is designed to develop personalized gene therapies more quickly.

“There are a lot of really good reasons to invest in domestic manufacturing capabilities, and Forge is a part of that,” she added.
But she also emphasized that people all around the world are impacted by the rare diseases that cell and gene therapies treat.
“Rare disease patient populations aren’t concentrated in any one country,” she said. “These are small communities; they’re distributed globally. For most of the diseases our clients are working on, the patients who need that therapy are spread across many geographies.”
While encouraged by ongoing discussions at and with the FDA about cell and gene therapy, Piteri-Molina cautions the industry against letting the case for domestic manufacturing narrow the industry’s perspective.
“The patient communities we’re ultimately serving are global ones,” she said, adding that the more stakeholders align, the better patients will be served.
“There are patient groups out there who every day are waiting to see . . . how quickly we get a treatment to them,” the Forge leader concluded. “It’s important for us to keep that in mind: what a privilege it is to do what we do, but also the responsibility that carries.”

After the FDA delayed a decision for Agios Pharmaceuticals’ sickle cell disease candidate, the biopharma is letting go of more than 35% of its R&D employees.
Agios Pharmaceuticals is axing over 35% of its R&D team in a commercial-focused restructuring that analysts view favorably.
The Massachusetts biopharma expects to incur about $11 million in restructuring charges this year, with savings from the 100-plus workforce reduction expected to be realized in 2027, according to a Thursday release . As of December 2025, Agios employed 539 full-time workers across its organization.
“Cost discipline provides another lever toward profitability,” Truist Securities wrote of Agios in a Thursday morning investor note. Agios now estimates it will turn a profit, excluding irregular or non-recurring costs, in 2028.
As part of the shift, Agios has “right sized” its operating model to align with its next phase of growth, CEO Brian Goff said on an earnings call on Thursday. This strategy is designed to “maximize the mitapivat franchise”—Agios’ oral pyruvate kinase activator that has secured approval in PK deficiency (sold as Pyrukynd ) and thalassemia (sold as Aqvesme ). Together, the mitapivat franchise earned $55.4 million in global net revenue for the third quarter, up 24% from last quarter and beating analysts’ consensus of $51.9 million.
Agios had been expecting an FDA decision for mitapivat in sickle cell disease by Nov. 1, but the agency pushed back its decision until Feb. 1, 2027, after requesting more information on a potential safety protocol for the drug.
Regulators were assessing whether a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) would be necessary for this indication and considered Agios’ response to its information request a major amendment to the drug application, according to an Oct. 30 release .
Both Pyrukynd and Aqvesme come with liver safety warnings, but only Aqvesme has a formal REMS program based on several liver adverse events occurring in thalassemia clinical testing. No similar hepatocellular injury cases have been observed in sickle cell disease thus far.
After the FDA delay, Agios’ stock sank more than 15% to $29.95 per share. Since then, the biotech’s shares have continued to slide, resting at $28.27 per share in premarket trading Friday.

Core logging at Perpetua Resources’ Stibnite gold-antimony project in Idaho. Credit: Perpetua Resources.
By: Staff Writer November 6, 2026
Perpetua Resources (Nasdaq: PPTA; TSX: PPTA) has discovered gold and antimony mineralization near a planned open pit at its Stibnite project in central Idaho, opening another exploration target as construction advances.
Discovery hole SB633 at the Fiddle target cut 109.7 metres grading 3.2 grams gold per tonne and 1.1% antimony from 189 metres depth, about 750 metres south of the permitted Yellow Pine pit, the company said in a Wednesday announcement .
“At Fiddle, our initial hole returned broad, continuous mineralization at significant gold and antimony grades which confirm it as an important new discovery,” CEO Jon Cherry said.
The discovery offers potential to expand the gold and antimony inventory near planned mining infrastructure. However, Fiddle has yet to become a defined mineral resource, and development outside the approved project would be subject to environmental review and permitting requirements.
Exploration results
Perpetua completed more than 16,000 metres of core drilling across Stibnite this season. The program tested new targets and extensions to known mineralization, while seeking to upgrade inferred resources within and near planned pits.
Fiddle lies along the Meadow Creek fault zone, which also runs through the Yellow Pine and Hangar Flats deposits. Follow-up hole SB637 extended mineralization 110 metres north of the discovery hole, cutting 37.4 metres grading 0.7 gram gold and 0.1% antimony from 93.8 metres depth.
Another 21 holes were drilled along the Fiddle trend. Results remain pending from two holes south of SB633, designated SB665 and SB671. Geologists observed similar mineralization in their core, but visual observations cannot establish whether they contain comparable grades or widths, Perpetua cautioned.
At the Clark Tunnel fault zone, drilling returned 25.4 metres grading 4.5 grams gold from 12.6 metres depth in hole SB606, and 25 metres at 2.3 grams from 18 metres depth in SB605. Antimony and tungsten assays remain pending.
The Clark Tunnel target lies partly within the permitted Yellow Pine pit and could supplement production during the project’s early years, the company said. The reported intersections are drill lengths rather than established true widths.
Construction advances
Stibnite’s estimated initial capital cost is $2.6 billion (C$3.6 billion), including contingency and before pre-production revenue, according to Perpetua’s updated project figures . The plan forecasts average annual gold production of 463,000 oz. during the first four years, compared with a stated life-of-mine annual average of 296,000 ounces.
Probable reserves total 104.6 million tonnes grading 1.43 grams gold and 0.064% antimony, containing about 4.8 million oz. gold and 149 million lb. antimony, as of last December, according to the company’s annual filing .
Stibnite holds the only identified U.S. antimony reserve, according to Perpetua. The metal has defence, energy and manufacturing applications.
Early works and construction of critical infrastructure have included the access road, worker housing and power infrastructure, Perpetua said in its September update . The U.S. Forest Service issued its principal project approval in January 2025, before President Donald Trump returned to office, followed by clearance to begin construction that October.
Perpetua shares were 8.6% stronger at $18.19 in Nasdaq trading on Friday morning, valuing the company at about $2.3 billion. The shares have traded between $15.66 and $37.37 over the past year.

Tall Boy Is a Stand-In Teardrop Trailer That's Cheap, Light, and Highly Modular
14 photos
Photo: Bend Teardrop
In a world of ultra-compact teardrop trailers that barely fit a double mattress inside, the Tall Boy makes for a surprising – and welcome – appearance. A teardrop that offers full standing height inside and accommodation for as many as five people depending on configuration, this trailer is what you could – and should – consider a must-see.
Tall Boy is the newest addition to the catalog of boutique-style Oregon-based Bend Teardrop, but it's not new. It debuted as a concept in late 2023 and made its way on the market in the flesh metal in February of the next year.
Since then, it's been a staple with this particular manufacturer and a hit with the customer base. Once you take into account all the pros working in its favor, it's not difficult to understand why. After all, the first thing that comes to mind when you say "teardrop trailer" is not the ability to stand up or a surprising degree of modularity.
And that brings us to the hottest selling point of this model, which has been refined constantly up to 2026: while still lightweight enough to be towed even by smaller vehicles and even moved into position by hand, it's tall enough to offer comfort comparable to a full-size travel trailer.
Photo: Bend Teardrop Tall Boy is built on the older Double Family model chassis, so you're looking at 16.5 feet (5 meters) of overall length, 7.1 feet (2.1 meters) of wheel-to-wheel width, and 8.3 feet (2.5 meters) of total height. That last one allows for 6.3 feet (1.92 meters) of interior headroom, so you can fully stand up inside.
A purist would argue that, despite the official description, Tall Boy is not a teardrop but rather a very compact travel trailer or, at best, a squaredrop . A purist would be right, but let's not let semantics get in the way of a nice product.
Tall Boy sits on a heavy-duty CNC-machined steel overland chassis, equipped with a single axle with spring leaf suspension. Construction is with an aluminum skinned shell, composite flooring, an aluminum-lined undercarriage, and an all-natural wood interior. Also standard, you get a pair of tinted slider windows and a couple of portholes, as well as a full-size entry door with a screen door.
Photo: Bend Teardrop As explained in the video tour at the bottom of the page and stated proudly on the official page, each Tall Boy is "built to suit." With a focus on an affordable edge over products from the competition, it comes standard with pretty much everything you need , but you can also customize it to whatever extent you want or can afford.
For instance, you can add independent suspension and beefier tires, or even an articulating hitch. That said, these upgrades will add to the cost of the final build, which will no longer be legitimately affordable.
You still have plenty to work with without the added expense, especially since this trailer is imagined as a family-friendly option that will either live at campsites or do mild boondocking – and little to no hardcore overlanding. Just for the interior, for example, you have four configurations possible.
Photo: Bend Teardrop You can choose bunk beds in front of the entrance with either an east-to-west double bed at the back or a California king that collapses into a couch during the day. You can add a removable table and you have dining and lounging taken care of. You can opt for either of these double beds and have a dinette instead at the front.
Depending on how you combine these, you can sleep up to five people inside, while still have some free floorspace to move around. The best part, according to the manufacturer, is that you also get storage for all these people, including under the two beds on the ground level.
Standard features inside include LED lights, power outlets and USB plugs, and you can opt to add more or change their standard location to suit your exact needs.
Photo: Bend Teardrop At the back, you get a sizable but basic tailgate galley . With the idea that everything has to be simple, affordable, and durable, Bend Teardrop puts here a stainless steel sink with a 2.5-gallon (9.5-liter) jug of water (you still have a faucet that will run city water if you hook up the trailer) and storage on a three-level arrangement.
This way, you get well compartmentalized storage, including a removable cutlery tray and a three-bottle built-in shelf. It might not seem like much, but it's the kind of thing that adds actual functionality to a space.
You also get 5.2 cu-ft (147 liters) of storage under the counter, where you also have space and a 12V plug for a cooler fridge. The extra large opening tailgate acts as weather protection, and you can add a separate hatch like the one in the unit below, for quicker access to the space under the counter.
Photo: Bend Teardrop Tall Boy "comes loaded" by default, in the sense that it's ready to go from the moment of delivery. By that, Bend Teardrop understands 200W of solar on the roof, trailer brakes, a 2-inch receiver hitch, AC shore power hookup with charger, the full door with lighted fold-out steps, a pass-through compartment at the back, a 10-speed two-way powered vent, a slide-in manual awning, and the upgraded galley.
Optionally , you can tweak just about everything, add a roof-mounted or a portable AC, a heater that will sit inside the pass-through storage compartment, a 12V TV, and a storage box or rack on the tongue. You can also have the manufacturer install a bike rack or further switch things up with the interior.
Photo: Bend Teardrop Whatever you add (or don't), the interior will be cottage-like, with real wood finishes on the walls, ceiling, and cabinetry.
The standard Tall Boy comes in at 1,995 lbs (905 kg) of dry weight, with just 150 lb (68 kg)of tongue weight, and a price of $22,950, which Bend Teardrop says is affordable given the kind of value and the quality of work you get.

Dealer Is Selling a Corvette ZR1X for $400,000 Over Sticker, Calls It by a Name That Doesn't Exist
12 photos
Photo: Abomination | X
A couple of photos have been making the rounds on the internet, taking the auto world by surprise. A dealership in Arkansas listed a 2027 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X with a $400,000 markup, calling it exclusive and naming it "Flagship Hypercar Edition," something that doesn't even exist.
The photos show how George Nunnally Chevrolet in Arkansas listed a 2027 Corvette ZR1X for sale with an unbelievable dealer markup , raising the asking price from the $296,445 MSRP all the way to a mind-blowing $696,445.
For the money, you could buy a Lamborghini Revuelto plug-in hybrid and still have money left for a Corvette Stingray. However, the dealership obviously got its hands on a motorized "treasure" and will by no means let it go without a fight. Or a markup. Or whatever.
The dealer tried to justify the extra money asked for the car, calling it the Flagship Hypercar Edition, which is not an actual edition, but a fabricated and absurd way of trying to artificially make the price of the ZR1X go through the roof.
Photo: Abomination | X The dealership refers to the silly markup as an "Exclusive Market Value Adjustment” and "Hypercar Demand Premium," and mentions "Extreme Exclusivity." True, it is an exclusive hypercar with zero inventory, being produced only on demand and coming with long waiting times.
Because production numbers are extremely tight and individual dealer allocations are rare, the vehicle has become a prime target for inflated dealership pricing and secondary car market flipping despite the 12-month resale ban imposed by General Motors through the purchase contract.
However, while General Motors heavily punishes flippers by voiding factory warranties if the cars are sold during the first year of ownership, it allows authorized dealerships to tack on a 135% markup with no problem whatsoever.
The Corvette ZR1X that the dealership in Arkansas is trying to sell rolled off the production line of the Bowling Green Assembly Plant in Kentucky with the 3LZ package . It is finished in the show-stopping Red Mist Metallic paint over a Jet Black interior.
Photo: Chevrolet With everything it's got on it, it would have dropped right under the $300,000 mark. For the money, customers willing to wait for months would get the exotic hypercar powered by the mighty twin-turbocharged 5.5-liter V8 and the front-mounted electric motor, pushing out a mind-blowing 1,250 horsepower (1,267 metric horsepower) and 973 pound-feet (1,320 Newton meters) of torque.
That is enough for the Corvette ZR1X to rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 1.89 seconds and run the quarter mile in 8.99 seconds, and max out at 233 mph (375 kph). After all, it is the car that lapped the Nürburgring in an incredible 6 minutes and 49.275 seconds, which makes it the second fastest American production car in the Green Hell.
Early listings and auctions have shown cars changing hands for anywhere between $312,000 and $550,000; George Nunally’s near-$700,000 is definitely an absurdity. The dealership probably expected this car to be sold quietly. Now, the whole internet knows about the dealer markup record. At the end of the day, the ZR1X is still a Chevy!
Other models that hit the market with massive dealer markups The Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X is by no means the only car that hit the market with massive dealer markups. Remember that the Tesla Cybertruck, which now has its days numbered, was there, too, back in late 2023 and early 2024, when it finally launched.
There was a time when a Porsche dealership listed the electric pickup truck for $249,000 when the starting price of the Foundation Series was around $100,000. In the meantime, Tesla tried to hunt down the flippers but gloriously failed.
Photo: Dodge 2023 was one Hell(cat) of a year for the car market. It was the year Dodge rolled out the Challenger SRT Demon 170 with 1,025 horsepower (1,039 metric horsepower). Dealerships routinely added markups between $100,000 and $250,000, despite Dodge trying to prioritize allocations to dealerships that promised to sell at sticker price.
Limited-run Porsche models have also been subject to markups over the years. The 911 Sport Classic saw markups as high as $250,000, while standard GT3 variants often see $100,000 tacked onto their $160,000 sticker prices.
It was the same for the Ford F-150 Lightning when it launched back in April 2022. The demand was so huge that dealerships wanted to ride the wave of popularity, prompting dealers to add $30,000 to $50,000 "market adjustments." In the meantime, Ford pulled the plug on the once-very-popular electric truck.
General Motors has been through this before, time and again. For instance, the early production GMC Hummer EV Edition 1 models were sold by dealers for $100,000+ over their original six-figure MSRP, with listings showing prices north of $250,000.
GM kept its distance back then, just like it did with the ZR1 without the X or the Z06. But now, it's maybe time it interfered. This Chevy dealer wants $400,000 over sticker for a Zr1x lmao https://t.co/bDhJKZ9iqY — Abomination (@Abomination81) October 30, 2026

Hanaa Is a Fully Custom Steel Yacht With an Unconventional Layout and Huge Sundeck
7 photos
Photo: Antonini Navi
Fully custom yachts represent the pinnacle of maritime luxury, offering clients the opportunity to develop a watercraft from a blank page and to create something that matches their vision of life at sea. Unlike production yachts, which are built using pre-designed plans, custom yachts are completely bespoke, with every aspect of the design, from the hull architecture to the amenities and interior finishes, designed to reflect how the owner wants to cruise and spend their time on board.
One of the shipyards that set out to offer yacht owners fully custom alternatives in an industry dominated by semi-custom designs is Antonini Navi. The renowned Italian shipyard is known for working with demanding clients who are used to the best things in life, and for pursuing luxury and innovation with each new vessel it designs. The latest project launched by the shipbuilder is Hanaa, a 31.2-meter (102-foot) superyacht that is set to be delivered to its owner in the spring of 2027.
Built with a steel hull and an aluminum superstructure, Hanna is a fully custom vessel based on Antonini’s Evo 31 motor yacht design and boasts naval architecture and exterior design by Hydro Tec and interiors by Milan-based studio Hot Lab. It was designed in close collaboration with the seasoned owners, who purposely sought the Antonini Navi shipyard in La Spezia for its experience.
The brief asked for an “attractive and modern” design with all the characteristics of an explorer yacht , such as long range, seaworthiness, and comfort for extended stays onboard. The yard delivered by creating a displacement motor yacht that spans four decks and offers spacious interior living quarters and generous outdoor areas, with an unconventional layout that enables a more informal way of living.
Photo: Antonini Navi For instance, instead of dedicating the main deck to a traditional formal salon and dining area, the owner wanted a large gathering space arranged around a central lounge that seamlessly flows into the aft cockpit and outdoor lounging spaces, creating an inviting environment for spending time with friends and family.
The forward area, which is typically occupied by the master suite in other yachts of this size, has been configured as a flexible, multifunctional space that can serve as an office, a meeting space, or a dining area, depending on the owners’ needs, and it also incorporates a private terrace. The result is an open, flexible deck that enables indoor-outdoor living.
The owner still benefits from sumptuous private quarters, but in this case, they are located on the upper deck, alongside the helm station. The master suite opens directly into a generous aft terrace, complete with a lounge, bar, and jacuzzi. This arrangement ensures the owner has plenty of privacy, keeping their suite separate from the four guest cabins, which are on the lower deck. Three cabins for crew are also located on the lower deck.
Another interesting choice in terms of interior layout is the location of the crew mess, which can be found on the main deck, with direct access to the galley for more streamlined daily operations.
Photo: Antonini Navi Penned by Hot Lab, the interiors have been designed in close collaboration with the owner and are described by the company as contemporary and welcoming, featuring organic shapes and natural materials.
Moving up to the sundeck, which spans over 78 square meters (839 square feet), we discover another welcoming living area, arranged with sunpads, al-fresco dining, and a barbeque. According to the yard, this is “one of the most spacious areas for socializing and relaxing in this category.”
The yacht also features a spacious engine room for easier maintenance and a side garage for a tender up to five meters (16 feet) long.
As for the exterior design, the team at Hydro Tec created a contemporary profile with clean lines, a bulbous bow, and long stretches of glazing intended to bring more natural light inside.
With a maximum beam of 7.5 meters (24.6 feet) and a full-load draught of 2.4 meters (8 feet), the yacht stays below the 300 GT mark, and according to the designers, the focus was on creating an efficient layout for comfortable extended stays within a more compact explorer profile.
Photo: Antonini Navi “With EVO 31, we wanted to break the mould and demonstrate that, even in this size category, we have the capabilities to build safe, modern, top-quality bespoke metal yachts, with interior and exterior liveability comparable to that of much larger vessels,” explained Antonini Navi.
“EVO 31 demonstrates that steel can be a viable alternative to fibreglass even for yachts of this size, representing a choice that offers strength, safety, the highest quality and great design freedom,” the team continued.
Hanaa is the second fully custom yacht built by the La Spezia-based shipyard, following the 33.5-meter (110-foot) Seamore 34 yacht Matilde 7, which was launched in July this year. Construction on this unit officially started with its keel-laying ceremony in January 2024, and its steel hull and aluminum superstructure are built to commercial construction standards, in accordance with MCA and Cayman Islands requirements.
Powered by two Caterpillar C18 engines rated at 533 Kw each, the custom yacht is expected to reach a maximum speed of 13 knots and a cruising speed of 12 knots, with a range of 4,000 nautical miles at ten knots.

ARRAY Technologies, a provider of structural balance-of-system (SBOS) solutions for utility-scale solar, and Shoals Technologies Group, which supplies electrical balance-of-system (EBOS) equipment for utility-scale solar and battery energy storage, said the companies have agreed to combine in a stock-for-stock merger. The firms on Nov. 4 said the deal “creates an integrated energy infrastructure platform that brings together complementary, market-leading solutions across foundations, trackers, fixed-tilt racking, electrical infrastructure, wire management and power delivery systems.”
The companies in a news release said ARRAY will serve as the corporate parent of the combined company. Shoals’ shareholders will receive a fixed exchange ratio of 1.6931 ARRAY shares for each Shoals’ share they own. After closing, Shoals’ shareholders are expected to own about 65% of the combined company’s basic shares outstanding, and ARRAY shareholders will own the rest.
Officials said the combined company will serve solar and battery energy storage customers through a unified design package, with coordinated purchasing and integrated warranty support across SBOS and EBOS solutions. The groups said the merger supports delivery of “increasing levels of integration over time designed to reduce installation costs, streamline project execution and lower long-term maintenance requirements.”
“Today marks an important milestone for Shoals, ARRAY and the customers we serve,” said Brandon Moss, CEO of Shoals. “By bringing together two highly complementary businesses with experienced teams, we are creating an integrated platform with broader capabilities, deeper customer relationships and a stronger foundation for long-term growth. We believe the combined company will be positioned to better service customers, deliver more innovative and integrated solutions, realize meaningful synergies and pursue expansion opportunities across the solar value chain, data center markets and beyond.”
Kevin Hostetler, ARRAY’s CEO, said, “This transaction represents a compelling opportunity to create meaningful value for customers of both ARRAY and Shoals by bringing together our complementary strengths. Although structural and electrical systems must operate seamlessly together in the field, they have historically been designed and sourced through separate channels. This combination changes that. Together, we expect to deliver a differentiated, technically integrated and interoperable platform that simplifies project execution, enhances project economics and accelerates innovation for customers.”
Strategic and Financial Rationale
The companies said the merger will bring several benefits for customers, including more effective service through a unified design package, with coordinated purchasing and integrated warranty support across combined offerings. The combined company intends to offer customers enhanced flexibility and packaging choice across foundations, trackers, electrical infrastructure and wire management solutions, including the solar industry’s best performing ground screw, single-axis tracker, DC wiring solution and cable management hanger.
The groups said customer value will be enhanced “by streamlining project execution, reducing installation costs, and lowering long-term maintenance requirements through increased product integration. SBOS and EBOS solutions are highly symbiotic across solar and battery storage projects. By bringing these complementary product categories together, the combined company expects to deliver more integrated solutions that reduce interface complexity, enhance energy yield and reliability, simplify installation and lower customers’ total cost of ownership.”
Officials also highlighted both companies technical expertise in their respective markets, which should support innovation. The combined company also expects to realize savings in overhead and other expenses, and noted “Year-one cost synergies are expected to deliver approximately $20 million of incremental, run-rate Adjusted EBITDA [Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization].” The combined company expects to benefit from Shoals’ approximately $1.6 billion of tax amortization and $237 million of Net Operating Losses, which are anticipated to reduce taxable income and limit the cash tax obligations of the combined company for the next several years.
Leadership Structure
Moss will serve as CEO of the combined company. Hostetler will serve as special advisor. Brad Forth, current chairman of the board of both ARRAY and Shoals, will serve as board chairman after the merger.
“Having had the privilege of serving as chairman of both ARRAY and Shoals, I have seen firsthand the complementary products, talented teams and shared commitment to customers offered by both companies,” said Forth. “Together, ARRAY and Shoals are well positioned to deliver enhanced value to customers, shareholders and employees. I also want to thank Kevin for his leadership and important contributions to ARRAY, as well as his valuable insights as he transitions to a Special Advisor role. I look forward to continuing to work with Brandon, who brings proven leadership, deep industry expertise and strategic vision to lead the combined company in this next phase of growth.”
The combined company intends to announce a new corporate name and ticker symbol in the coming months to reflect the expanded scope of its products, services and strategic opportunities.

Ninety-one percent of materials handling professionals surveyed by Modern Materials Handling said they like their current job , up from 88% a year earlier. In the same survey, 88% described their job as at least somewhat stressful.
What’s Related
The 2026 survey also found that 97% would recommend materials handling as a career, the highest share in four years. Fifty-two percent said they were very satisfied with their career, and another 22% were extremely satisfied.
Peerless Research Group surveyed 117 qualified Modern Materials Handling subscribers for the 19th annual study. Manufacturing accounted for the largest share of respondents. The survey also included people working in wholesale and retail trade , transportation and warehousing .
“People who are in materials handling and supply chain really love the profession, and there’s lots of room for growth and opportunity,” said Michelle Rohlwing, innovation, product development and learning manager at the Institute for Supply Management .
RELATED: 2026 Salary Survey: Average Materials Handling Pay Dips Under $100K | What Logistics and Supply Chain Jobs Pay in 2026
Too much work
Among respondents who called their jobs very or extremely stressful, 42% pointed to workload, the most common answer for the third year in a row. Too few people to get the job done and outdated technology tied for second, each cited by 35%.
Across all respondents, 53% called their jobs somewhat stressful, 26% described them as very stressful, and 9% called them extremely stressful. The remaining 12% said their jobs were either not very stressful or not stressful at all.
Among those who described their jobs as very or extremely stressful, concern about company stability rose more than any other factor. Twenty-two percent cited it, up from 7% in 2025. The share who pointed to a lack of career development fell from 25% to 16%, and 3% cited a poor relationship with their boss, down from 8%.
Longtime workers show loyalty
Respondents averaged 18.5 years in materials handling. Nearly a third had spent 20 to 29 years in the field, and another 19% had spent 30 years or more. Seventeen percent had less than five years of experience.
They stayed with their employers, too, averaging 10.4 years with their current company. Twenty-eight percent had been there for at least 20 years. Respondents had worked for an average of 2.7 companies over their materials handling careers, and 16% had worked for only one.
Three more findings from the survey
Job satisfaction and career satisfaction moved in different directions. The share who liked their current job rose from 88% to 91%, while the share who were very or extremely satisfied with their career fell from 78% to 74%.
Work pressure carried over into home life. Among respondents who described their jobs as very or extremely stressful, 34% cited balancing work and home life, and 29% said they didn’t have enough time to get their work done.
Management decisions added to the pressure. In that same group, 31% cited questionable management decisions, up from 28% in 2025.

Audi Finally Ends A8 Luxury Sedan Production After 32 Years, New Gen Under Consideration
16 photos
Photo: Audi
Audi's 7 Series and S-Class fighter spent more than three decades making its case for German engineering and luxury in a full-size package. Unfortunately, the A8 has left the Neckarsulm factory that built every generation since its debut.
The plant stopped making A8s in October 2026, now focusing on the A5 line of sedans and wagons. Ingolstadt, however, is working out what comes next for its flagship luxobarge. Its canning did not happen overnight, for Audi stopped accepting new orders for the full-size model in February 2026.
This left customers to choose from available inventory, which is a big no-no in this particular segment where options and customization are of the essence. As of this writing, the A8 is marketed for the 2027 model year in the US market. Back in March 2026, namely one month after Ingolstadt pulled the plug on it, Audi made it clear that a new generation is under consideration.
To be revealed by decade's end, the newcomer could be a very different animal from the last generation. For starters, Audi could very well use the Volkswagen Group architecture of the next-generation Panamera. That model is due to enter series production at Porsche's Leipzig facility around 2030, and sharing underpinnings clearly makes financial sense.
A different proposal comes from German business publication Manager Magazin, which reports that Audi has considered a luxury sedan for the Chinese market. Huawei, together with either FAW or SAIC, would give Audi established technology and manufacturing relationships.
Photo: Audi The People's Republic of China is a very interesting recipient, be it a Volkswagen Group design or something developed in collaboration with local heavyweights. Large and luxurious sedans retain a strong market position there, much stronger than in Western markets, but such a China-focused A8 would make little sense if Audi cannot tailor it according to Chinese preferences.
While Audi may still consider a flagship sedan important enough to develop, its future production arrangements remain under discussion. For the time being, the Q9 sport utility vehicle serves as the brand's series-production flagship. At the other end of the spectrum, the Nuvolari supercar is best described as the German brand's take on the V8-powered Lamborghini Temerario.
Currently priced at $95,100 in the US market, the A8 comes with the S line exterior, OLED taillights, and 22-way comfort front seats by default. Its base powertrain is the group's familiar 3.0-liter turbocharged V6, which offers 335 horsepower and plenty of torque from low engine speeds. Due to quattro all-wheel drive, 60 miles per hour (97 kilometers per hour) takes only 5.6 seconds.
The much pricier S8 can do a lot better, though. Gifted with a V8, the performance-oriented version packs 563 horsepower and 590 pound-feet (800 Newton-meters) of twist, enough to propel the European luxobarge to 60 in a mere 3.8 seconds. This generation of the A8 is called D5, and can you believe that Audi started making it nine years ago?
Whatever the future holds for the A8, rival automakers Mercedes and BMW are likely happy that Audi is no longer an option in this particular segment. As it stands, the Sonderklasse and the 7 Series have only the Genesis G90 and the outgoing Lexus LS to worry about.

Mercedes and its AMG division have found another way to sell the appeal of the MANUFAKTUR customization program. On this occasion, the happy customer happens to be the winner of a tennis tournament. Described as a one-off, this SL 55 4MATIC+ is destined for the WTA Finals champ.
Beautified with ultraviolet paintwork over white Nappa leather, the 55 in question boasts a bunch of personalized goodies that connect it to the Women's Tennis Association. The roadster was unleashed in the flesh at Merc's Brand Studio in Beverly Hills right before the competition starts in Indian Wells.
As you can tell from the shots provided by none other than Mercedes , the exterior does most of the talking. The look-at-me paintwork is a MANUFAKTUR Made to Measure finish inspired by the WTA's purple. 21-inch AMG forged cross-spoke wheels add no subtlety whatsoever. On the contrary, these wheels make the German roadster even more audacious.
Subtlety, however, was never the assignment. In fact, Merc was fully aware that it had to deliver a car that looks precisely like a tournament prize before anyone gets close enough to see its Mercedes-Benz and Mercedes-AMG badging. This audacity continues inside, where Crystal White MANUFAKTUR Nappa leather does the talking by creating a sharp contrast.
AMG carbon-fiber trim pieces add to the visual drama, bringing some darker surfaces into the mix. WTA Finals embossing and engraving remind the owner that she did not simply take delivery of just another 55. The special treatment continues with custom door sills and a special badge that will ultimately carry the winner's name, giving this SL an identity of its own, beyond the crazy paint job and the superb-looking upholstery.
Photo: Mercedes-AMG There is, however, a problem with this car that I cannot ignore. Why 55 and not the 63 or something even more special? For model year 2027, the AMG SL range is topped by a plug-in hybrid with ridiculous torque, and this powertrain is exactly what I would expect from such a collab between the Stuttgart-based automaker and the Women's Teams Association.
It gets worse once you remember that Mercedes and the AMG division also gave Maybach a shot at the SL. While it may not be as punchy as the AMG-ified 63 S E PERFORMANCE, the 680 Monogram Series is an ultra-luxury interpretation of the rear-biased roadster from Bremen.
Despite not being tuned for superlative performance, 4.0 seconds flat to 60 miles per hour (97 kilometers per hour) is properly quick. As of this writing, the 2027 model year Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series will set you back a cool $225,900 before destination and optional extras. All in all, yeah, limiting the tournament prize to the AMG SL 55 4MATIC+ is a bit strange.
And looking at the bigger picture, this car exists because this partnership gives Mercedes a visible way to connect its name with a very popular sport and women. BMW's rival entered the 2026 season as a Premier Partner and Exclusive Automobile Partner of the WTA Tour, with this arrangement including the Signature Court, digital content, and experiences designed specifically to bring the brand closer to tennis fans.
The singles champion won't be the only player receiving something from Mercedes. Per the WTA, each member of the winning doubles team will receive a complimentary 12-month lease of a Mercedes-Benz vehicle. That being said, the 2026 FAGE WTA Finals run from November 8, 2026, through November 15, 2026, and this edition marks the competition's first visit to the California venue.
